title: Orion Retail - Ops & Efficiency Playback

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-14
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Sofia (Orion Head of AI), Liam (Platform Eng), Hannah (Finance), Rajiv (CTO)
Meeting ID: ff-20261014-orion-7234

Summary (auto): quick playback of Sep incident, cost breakout, and holiday readiness.

00:00 - Maya: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, we'll do a quick run through of what we saw in September, some cost notes, and then talk about next steps for Black Friday prep.
00:22 - Sofia: great thanks Maya, yep we had a couple of headaches with latency spikes and the finance team is, yeah, a little worried about the bill creep.
00:35 - Ethan: quick clarifying q — is the spike primarily coming from embeddings/semantic search or generation endpoints?
00:47 - Liam: mostly generation, the product team rolled out a new chat flow that doubled average tokens per session, so token count shot up. Also we had a bad caching config, i think someone disabled prefix caching during a deploy — so K V cash wasnt kicking in.
01:10 - Maya: okay so two levers: reduce tokens per call or enable better caching; both have different tradeoffs on latency and UX.
01:22 - Hannah: finance — the main worry is the unpredictability, we like the committed capacity pricing but the burst behavior surprised us last month.
01:35 - Rajiv: quick note — we are evaluating Dedicated pools for holiday traffic but need to understand warm up times and failover to hosted. can you run a cost delta for 2 weeks Dedicated vs hosted burst?
01:48 - Maya: yes, we'll model that. Ethan, can you capture the warm up / kv cache warm-rate numbers?
01:55 - Ethan: yeah i'll add that to the soak checklist, but just flag: warm up depends a lot on seq len distribution and kv cache hit rates, so we need representative windows.
02:10 - Speaker 3 (transcription may be off): also saw a spike in 3rd-party auth calls causing latency, S S O handshake delays.
02:28 - Sofia: correct — we saw some auth latency that cascaded; simultaneous, the region failover hit a small network blip.
02:40 - Maya: can you remind us the SLA line items you need? uptime, p99 latency, cost predictability?
02:49 - Sofia: top priorities: 99.95 uptime, p99 < 600ms for chat endpoints in EU/US, and clear monthly spend caps + alerting.
02:59 - Ethan: for p99<600ms we'll probably recommend a mix: pin some critical routes to dedicated nodes and keep lower-tier traffic on hosted. routing policies can do that.
03:14 - Liam: question on private deployment: we may need VPC peering with our on-prem identity provider, and KMS integration for keys — any gotchas?
03:25 - Maya: we have a private deployment playbook — RSA note: keys can be customer-managed via KMS/HSM, and audit logs are available; i'll share the SOC2 extract and KMS integration guide after this call.
03:39 - Hannah: ok thanks, please make sure finance sees the integration pricing impacts.
03:47 - Ethan: also, small nuance — when you go Dedicated you lose some auto-burst elasticity unless you keep a small hosted fallback; so the recommended architecture is hybrid: base RPS on Dedicated + hosted spillover.
04:05 - Rajiv: for the September outage, can you summarize the RCA? who owns what?
04:14 - Maya: quick RCA summary: a config rollback during a deploy inadvertently disabled auto-caching for a subset of endpoints; concurrently, an auth provider degraded, which increased request time; combined, these increased queuing and caused CPU infra stress on a subset of nodes. We implemented a fallback policy and rolled back the change.
04:36 - Sofia: was this related to the new routing rules we pushed?
04:41 - Ethan: partly — the routing change meant more cross-zone traffic and we had a subtle kernel-level scheduling spike— transcription note: kernel sched or kit el? — that caused uneven load. we've mitigations checked in: more conservative routing rollout and improved tracing.
05:05 - Maya: action: we'll set stricter canary windows for routing changes and add an immediate rollback playbook.
05:15 - Liam: what are the mitigation timelines if we start a pilot for Dedicated — how long to provision and validate?
05:25 - Ethan: typical lead time is 48-72 hours to provision committed slots, then 3-5 days to warm with realistic traffic; for full validation we'd recommend a 2-week soak with traffic replay.
05:40 - Sofia: two-week soak sounds ideal but business wants estimates ASAP — Hannah, can you confirm budget?
05:50 - Hannah: we can provision but need a capped overage scenario and clear reporting; otherwise we get pushback.
05:59 - Maya: we'll provide a pricing scenario: committed monthly vs two-week dedicated and hosted fallback with overage caps and alert thresholds.
06:12 - Speaker 2 (maybe Ethan): on cost optimizations, we've seen wins by quantization and reduce tokenization; but you should validate quality degradation. Redwood Optimize can run model/quant recommendations per workload.
06:32 - Sofia: is there any immediate quick win before Black Friday?
06:39 - Ethan: enable prefix/KV caching and adjust batch windows — small latency increase for some calls but big token cost reduction. Also review prompt templates to trim unnecessary context.
06:51 - Sofia: we'll get sample prompts.
06:56 - Rajiv: security — confirm SOC2, ISO? can you produce certs and details on logging retention?
07:06 - Maya: yes, SOC2 Type II artifact is available; ISO pending for Partner region but we have audit logs retention configurable per account; i'll attach the specifics.
07:20 - Liam: for KMS we need HSM-backed keys and rotation policy compatibility.
07:27 - Ethan: supported, but customer-managed rotation is in your control; Redwood can integrate with common KMS providers (notes: aws-kms, gcp-kms, azure keyvault).
07:40 - Hannah: finance question — what's the commit minimum for Dedicated?
07:45 - Maya: there's a monthly minimum depending on region and GPU class; i'll include numbers in the pricing sheet. for pilot we can do a shorter timebox.
07:56 - Sofia: about monitoring — can we get per-model token breakdowns and per-route spend in the console?
08:05 - Ethan: yes, per-route/model dashboards are available and we can set token-level alerts and trace hooks. we'll give you a sample dashboard link.
08:18 - Rajiv: do you have recommendations for preventing the auth cascades we saw?
08:24 - Maya: circuit breakers for auth failures, local caching of tokens, and fallback auth endpoints. we'll document the recommended patterns.
08:34 - Sofia: ok, i'd like to propose two pilots: 1) cost optimization sweep (7 days) focused on caching/quantization and prompt trims; 2) Dedicated 2-week soak for peak traffic window before Black Friday.
08:48 - Maya: we can do both. propose we kick off the cost sweep first to get immediate wins, then the Dedicated soak.
08:57 - Hannah: budget okay for two pilots if we get clear ROI estimates.
09:05 - Ethan: for the cost sweep we'll need sample traffic traces and representative prompt sets, please redact PII.
09:13 - Sofia: i'll prepare a traffic window and send it by Monday.
09:18 - Speaker 4 (auto): [link] Orion - traffic-sample-2026-09.zip (shared in chat)
09:25 - Maya: great — action items noted. any other questions?
09:30 - Liam: one more on deployment rollback — can we have a runbook that triggers automatic fallback to hosted in case Dedicated nodes degrade?
09:39 - Ethan: yes, routing policies support automatic fallback; we'll template a policy that responds to p99/p95 thresholds and error rates.
09:50 - Sofia: last thing, can you share the SLA wording around cost and overages? we want to include it in procurement.
09:58 - Maya: i'll attach procurement-friendly wording and the legal template.
10:04 - Rajiv: timeline recap?
10:09 - Maya: Okay recap: Redwood to share SOC2, KMS guide, and procurement SLA by 2026-10-18. Maya to send pricing sheet by 2026-10-16. Ethan to produce dedicated-soak checklist and runbook by 2026-10-20. Orion to share traffic windows and sample prompts by 2026-10-18. Pilot start target: week of 2026-10-25 pending confirmations.
10:34 - Sofia: sounds good. thanks for the quick turnaround.
10:40 - Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and links to the docs.
10:45 - Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: some speaker labels and tech terms may be mis-transcribed (e.g., K V cache, V P C spelled out). There was a short crosstalk during the RCA section that caused a few words to garble.
